reasoning: Recent polling and coverage of Nebraska’s 1st congressional district general-election House race consistently show Republican Rep. Mike Flood leading Democrat Chris Backemeyer by mid-single digits, with aggregation of three polls through mid‑May yielding about an R+5.7 environment in the district.[6][7] Forecaster-style and ratings coverage still describe the race or district as “Solid R,” but national Democrats have moved NE‑01 into their “districts in play” program, suggesting a competitive but still GOP‑favored race; together this points to a current general‑election margin of roughly R+5–6 in NE‑01.[1][6][7][14] The statewide structural Cook PVI for Nebraska is R+10, indicating a substantially Republican baseline at the state level.[3]

sources.name: PredictionEdge (poll aggregation for NE‑01 House)
sources.details: PredictionEdge’s NE‑01 page, aggregating three general-election House polls (Tavern Research and Zenith Research) through May 8‑19, reports Flood leading Backemeyer by an average of 5.7 points (Flood 43.7%, Backemeyer 38.0%, Ahlman 9.0%), described as “Flood+5.7.”

sources.name: Plains Sentinel (Zenith and Tavern Research poll write‑up for NE‑01)
sources.details: Plains Sentinel summary of polling notes a Zenith Research poll of the NE‑01 House race showing Flood leading Backemeyer 43–34 with an independent candidate at 10%, characterizing Flood as having “a slight edge” and citing Cook Political’s view of the district as Solid Republican, leaning +6 GOP.

sources.name: Tavern Research (NE‑01 House general-election poll, as summarized)
sources.details: Within the same Plains Sentinel coverage, an individual Tavern Research general-election poll for NE‑01 is reported with Flood ahead of Backemeyer, including a cited spread such as Flood+8 in one test and Flood+2 in another, reinforcing a modest but consistent Republican lead.

sources.name: Sabato’s Crystal Ball 2026 House ratings (NE‑01)
sources.details: Sabato’s Crystal Ball 2026 House ratings list Nebraska’s 1st congressional district as a strongly Republican seat (Solid/likely R), indicating clear GOP advantage even though not providing a numeric margin.
sources.date_range: through July 10, 2025 (rating still referenced in 2026 coverage)

sources.name: QuiverQuant NE‑01 election profile
sources.details: QuiverQuant’s profile of Nebraska’s 1st congressional district election notes that the race rating is currently “Solid R,” reflecting a strong Republican advantage without giving a specific vote-margin estimate.

sources.name: Nebraska Examiner via 1011 Now (DCCC “districts in play” story)
sources.details: Nebraska Examiner/1011 Now report that the DCCC has placed Nebraska’s 1st district in its “districts in play” program, describing the Flood–Backemeyer race as competitive enough for national Democratic investment but not asserting that Democrats are favored.

sources.name: Newsweek (Tavern Research poll context in Nebraska)
sources.details: Newsweek, in discussing Tavern Research polling in Nebraska, references a competitive Nebraska race but its detailed numbers (47–42) are for the statewide Senate race and not NE‑01, providing contextual evidence of GOP vulnerability but not district-specific margins.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – 2026 Cook Partisan Voting Index (state table)
sources.details: The 2026 Cook Partisan Voting Index table lists Nebraska’s statewide PVI as R+10, indicating that in recent presidential elections the state has voted about 10 points more Republican than the national average.
